Uh, are you all in? We're about to start. Because of the epidemic, we're all working from home, so the Internet might not be good. Don't be surprised—I'm in Shanghai, Minhang, at home right now. A lot of my colleagues are at home, and so are my roommates. If you're all here, then let's start. ## Suit Design Overview We're going to talk about how to make a suit. This suit consists of a two-layer material and an outer fabric with a two-layer structure. ### Downloading the Model First of all, we're going to download a version of the suit. If it's a version, you can just confirm it. Next, we're going to download a virtual model. You can choose one of your favorite models. After you download it, select the version. ### Copying and Arranging Panels We need to copy the other side of the version using Control + D. Make sure to copy the version with the colon. After we copy it, we will put the corresponding version together. This will make it easier for us to sort and arrange it later. ### Using the 2D/3D Tool Bar Next, click on the 2D/3D toolbar. From the 2D arrangement tool, we will add two layers of the board and put it all together. You can see the effect on the screen. After the selection, adjust the locator. Right-click in the blank to select one locator with a world coordinate. This way, if you move the angle, its coordinate direction will not change. ## Working with Panels We will look at the small panels, like the pocket panel, and the elastic strips. We won’t do anything with these panels first; just save it. After saving, you can see the 3D window, and this panel will be gone. We can skip the simulation for now and put it down. ### Sleeve Panel Adjustment Next, we will adjust the sleeve panel inside. We’ll put it back because the ball is blue. Make a single adjustment, and the other side will be the same. Move to overlap, push it back, and adjust the single panel on the side as well. ### Button Panel Arrangement Now, let’s take a look at the button panel. We have to choose it before we arrange it. Depending on your actual situation, you can arrange it for pre and post arrangements. On my side, it’s from left to right, so I’ll move the left panel to the front. ### Finalizing Panel Arrangements Next, we will arrange all panels. Select the front panel and find a suitable arrangement. After arranging it, we can use this frame to adjust its size and move its position with the positioning ball. The sleeves will be the same; choose the two layers of sleeves together and find an arrangement in the back. ### Adjusting the Collar For the collar, if it’s too tight, you can adjust the diameter. After all arrangements are done, let’s move to the 2D window for powdering. A more important point is that you have to sew the knife to the knife because the suit requires precision. ## Sewing the Suit When sewing, start with the side seam and the sleeves on both sides. The back seam requires accuracy, so try to sew the knife to the knife as much as possible. This includes powdering on the knife as well as the door and the material. ### Shoulder and Collar Sewing We will sew the shoulder first. If there is a knife opening, try to sew to that point. The same goes for the back of the sleeve. After sewing, change the sewing line type to a fold seam for a more even simulation. ### Connecting Lines Next, we will connect the basic line to the inner line, changing it to a 360-degree angle. This is crucial for the fold. After connecting, we will set the seam line type to a fold for a zero-degree effect on both sides. ## Final Adjustments After selecting a piece of material, it only folds inwards on one side. This is because these pieces are connected, so we will remove the connection and hook it up with a hook tool. ### Adjusting the Collar Again Let's check the collar again; if it needs adjustment, we can turn it over. After adjusting, we can see the intersection before and after. ## Simulation Preparation Before simulating, we will select all panels and print them. This is necessary due to the folds and angles. If the simulation doesn’t look right, we can unlock buttons or adjust angles to ensure better stability. ### Button and Zipper Simulation To simulate, we need to add a button. Select the button tool in the 3D window and click to add a button. After adding, select the button and copy it to the layer for a quick duplication. ## Simulation Execution Before we simulate, ensure that all panels are selected. The simulation may not be perfect, so we need to check for any issues, like buttons being blocked or instability in the simulation. ### Opening the Suit For the opening effect of the suit, we can freeze the model to prevent other parts from moving. Then, unlock the button and frame to simulate the opening effect. ## Conclusion After all adjustments and simulations, we can finalize the suit design. Remember, this process takes practice to perfect. For any further details or questions, feel free to reach out in the live broadcast room or through our public account. Thank you for joining this lesson, and happy designing! ```
